title: India and Egypt agree to scope a trade pact; Cairo offers Indian firms a Suez base
dek: At the seventh India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee in Cairo, the commerce ministers agreed to draw up terms for a preferential or free trade agreement, and Egypt offered Indian companies a dedicated zone near the Suez Canal.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India and Egypt agreed on Sunday to begin work on the terms of a possible trade agreement, as Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal led more than 130 Indian business leaders and start-up founders to Cairo for the seventh meeting of the two countries' Joint Trade Committee.

Mr Goyal said officials on both sides would be tasked with drawing up terms of reference to examine either a preferential trade agreement, which cuts tariffs on a limited list of goods, or a fuller free trade agreement. Egypt's Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, Mohamed Farid Saleh, who co-chaired the meeting, offered Indian companies land in a dedicated zone in the Suez Canal Economic Zone or elsewhere in the country, according to reports of the business forum that followed.

## What happened

The Joint Trade Committee, the ministerial forum that reviews trade between the two countries, met in Cairo on Sunday, 15 November, the government said in a release ahead of the visit. Mr Goyal arrived on Saturday for a two-day official visit aimed, the release said, at deepening the India-Egypt strategic partnership through trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

Speaking at the India-Egypt Business Forum after the committee met, Mr Goyal said the two sides would "task our officials to work on the terms of reference" for a trade agreement, according to reports. He said such a pact could give businesses on both sides better access to each other's markets and let them trade on more competitive terms. The ministers also discussed closer cooperation between customs authorities and mutual recognition agreements under which each side would accept the other's testing agencies, a step that can cut the cost and delay of certifying goods.

Mr Saleh said he hoped the two countries would be signing a preferential trade agreement, free trade agreement or comprehensive economic partnership agreement by the next meeting of the committee, which is due in New Delhi in 2028, according to reports. On the offer of a shared industrial zone, he said: "We had agreed on many things, but this I'm putting on the table for the businesses to decide."

Mr Goyal urged Indian companies to use Egypt as a base to reach Africa, the Middle East and Europe, telling them to "visit the Suez Canal Economic Zone", and said he would ask colleagues in New Delhi to look at the sites on offer. He named affordable medicines, generics, vaccines, biosimilars and medical devices among the areas where India could do more, and urged both sides to match Egypt's 12 to 13 priority sectors with Indian strengths.

The two countries are due to sign a start-up partnership agreement on Monday and hold the first Egypt-India Startup Forum, Mr Goyal said. His programme also includes a meeting of the India-Egypt Joint Business Council, talks with senior Egyptian ministers and a meeting with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the government said. On Saturday he paid tribute at Cairo's Heliopolis War Cemetery, where 3,727 of the roughly 4,000 soldiers buried or commemorated are Indian, and addressed the Indian community, which he called "a living bridge between the two countries".

## Background

Trade between India and Egypt is worth about $6.5 billion a year, according to the government, and Mr Goyal said on Sunday that this fell well short of what the two economies could achieve. Commerce ministry figures show it is rising fast: merchandise trade grew 64% year on year to $5.04 billion in April to September 2026, according to reports citing the data. In the financial year 2025-26, India exported goods worth $3.87 billion to Egypt and imported goods worth $2.60 billion. Machinery and petroleum products were India's main exports; crude oil and fertilisers were its main imports.

Nearly 70 Indian companies operate in Egypt, with investments of more than $5 billion, the government said.

India and Egypt raised their relationship to a strategic partnership in 2023. India has no trade agreement with Egypt today, and the terms of reference agreed on Sunday are only the first step: they set out what a negotiation would cover before formal talks begin.

## Why it matters for India

Egypt controls the Suez Canal, the shortest sea route between India and Europe, and the canal's economic zone sits on the shipping lane that carries much of India's trade with Europe and the Mediterranean. Attacks on shipping in the Red Sea in recent years have at times pushed many ships onto the much longer route around Africa, raising freight costs for Indian exporters; a manufacturing base on the canal would give Indian firms a foothold on the European side of that bottleneck.

Egypt is also an important market for Indian medicines and a supplier of fertilisers, which India imports in large volumes to keep farm costs down. A trade deal would add Egypt to the list of trade agreements India has been negotiating in recent years. Mr Saleh's offer of land for Indian companies comes as several countries, including China, are investing in industrial zones along the canal.

## What they are saying

Mr Goyal, on the trade pact: officials will "work on the terms of reference" and examine the potential of either a preferential or a free trade agreement.

Mr Saleh, on the industrial zone: "We had agreed on many things, but this I'm putting on the table for the businesses to decide."

Mr Goyal, on the Indian community in Egypt: "a living bridge between the two countries".

## What happens next

- 16 November: start-up partnership agreement to be signed in Cairo; first Egypt-India Startup Forum; Mr Goyal's visit ends.
- Officials from both countries are to draft terms of reference for a preferential or free trade agreement; no date has been set.
- Indian ministries are to review the sites offered in the Suez Canal Economic Zone.
- 2028: the eighth meeting of the Joint Trade Committee is due in New Delhi.

## Key numbers

- About $6.5 billion: annual India-Egypt trade, according to the government
- $5.04 billion: merchandise trade in April-September 2026, up 64% year on year
- $3.87 billion: India's exports to Egypt in 2025-26
- $2.60 billion: India's imports from Egypt in 2025-26
- Nearly 70: Indian companies operating in Egypt, with more than $5 billion invested
- 130+: business leaders and start-ups travelling with Mr Goyal
